brief: GS's ETF flow desk reports on Thursday November 5's session, when the Nasdaq-100 fell 5.5%, its worst day since March 2020 and a multi-sigma event, with elevated volumes continuing into Friday morning. US-listed ETF notional volume hit $580 billion, the third-largest day on record and 33% of total market volume versus a 28% average; several products set records, including QQQ ($86bn), combined SOXL/SOXS ($37bn+) and MAGS ($890mm), while XLV traded its busiest session in over a year. Within the levered/inverse ETF complex, net inflows totaled $1.1 billion as levered funds gained $3.3 billion and inverse funds lost $2.2 billion, the widest dispersion on record; the note cites a historical pattern of levered-ETF inflows peaking on down days and troughing on up days. Despite that inflow, complex-wide AUM and gross exposure have fallen $55 billion and $135 billion respectively over the trailing 20 days. Numerous names (NDX, semis, Korea, growth, momentum) hit six-month lows, while defensive proxies (utilities, min-vol, staples, retail, healthcare) extended multi-week outperformance and inflow streaks.
